subject: koala
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: koala gripping a eucalyptus branch stand.
Style: pixel art.
reasoning:
I'm planning a compact pixel-art module featuring a koala hugging a eucalyptus trunk pole on a wooden stand base, with a simple but present skeleton rig for the rest pose.

I'm working out coordinates so the koala faces the viewer while its arms and legs wrap backward around the trunk, sizing the body, head, and stand proportions, then planning to use cellPaint texturing with box and sweep primitives to achieve the chunky pixel look.

Now I'm setting up the joint hierarchy: a hips root, a spine chain curving from hips to chest to neck base, then separate head and jaw joints attached at the spine's tip, before starting the body sweep along that spine chain.

Adding claw details to the hands, then setting up the legs with hips, feet, and thigh bends parented to the hip joints. For the head I'm placing the head box, a large dark nose/muzzle, and upper jaw pieces using model-space offsets since the head faces forward.

Continuing head details... lower jaw on its own joint, fluffy round ears with white inner decal boxes, small black eye boxes positioned on the head front, plus a pixel-art eye texture plane for a glint highlight. I'm also planning a lighter countershaded belly using cell-paint fur edges.

Now I'm setting up the stand: a wooden plank base, a vertical trunk sweep with a hexagonal bark-textured cross-section, and two angled branch stubs near the top holding scattered pixel-art leaf cards for foliage.

Trunk runs from 0.06 to 1.3, with koala hips around y=.4 floating as if gripping the trunk. That seems good enough to finalize.
